root_cause: scc 4.1.0 counts the // line inside a Java raw-string literal (text block) as a comment even though it is raw-string content; this is a known scc limitation documented in tests/metrics/run.py
scc 4.1.0 counts the // line inside a C# raw-string literal as a comment even though it is raw-string content; this is a known scc limitation documented in tests/metrics/run.py

Standalone scc 4.1.0 classifies C header files (.h) as 'C Header' grammar and counts #ifdef/#if/#elif/#else preprocessor branches as complexity contributions. dircue's embedded scc uses the 'C' grammar for the same files, which counts fewer complexity keywords. The code/comment/blank/lines counts agree; only complexity differs. This is a grammar-selection difference, not a counting bug.

Standalone scc 4.1.0 classifies Helm template .tpl files as 'Smarty Template' grammar. dircue classifies them as 'Go Template' (more accurate for Helm/Go text/template syntax). The comment syntax {{/* ... */}} is parsed differently: dircue correctly recognizes these as comments; scc's Smarty grammar does not. Code/comment counts differ due to this grammar selection difference, not a counting error.

Standalone scc 4.1.0 classifies .t files as 'Raku' (Perl 6) by extension, even when the file starts with #!/bin/bash and is a shell script. dircue uses the shebang to classify these as 'Shell'. The complexity counts differ because Raku and Shell grammars have different complexity-keyword sets. dircue's classification is more accurate for shebang-identified shell test scripts.
